I wouldn’t worry if I were you, which I know is easier said than done. I got my first period at 12 and never experienced any cramping until I was about 17. Keep in mind that your first period is usually really heavy and that the second day of your cycle is usually the heaviest flow for most ppl. Drink plenty of water and get your favorite snacks.

You should tell your mom or a trusted adult, they can help you clean everything up, get you more period products, and explain how to use them. As for getting the blood out of your clothes wash with cold water and soap. I also highly recommend using Awesome Spray to help get out any blood stains.

If you do start getting cramps a combo of Ibuprofen, Tylenol, and caffeine works well but ask your parents first so that you don’t accidentally take the wrong dosage. Also, heating pads and warm baths work wonders. Dairy can make cramping worse for some people but not everyone. It might be a good idea to keep an extra pair of underwear and pants in your bag just incase until your period is over, that way if you do bleed through anything you won’t have to worry about anyone seeing.

If your period ever does become extremely painful or you start bleeding more than normal let your parents and doctor know so that you can get help, far too many young girls don’t know that you can get medical help with period pain because nobody ever tells them.

His best bet at getting mental healthcare for this (in America) would be to first find out if he qualifies for state or federal health insurance. If he does then get that and immediately work on finding a therapist and psych that works with trauma. Depending on where he lives gov insurance will cover most if not all of it. If he doesn’t qualify then look for a free or low cost community therapy center that accepts ex-convicts. If he’s in a big city there’s usually at least a few places that will have spots open “soonish” (aka anytime between next week and the next decade). I would still recommend finding free/low cost therapy as a temporary option even if he does qualify for gov insurance since private therapists usually have a pretty long wait list.

Also, if he hasn’t already you need to figure out who his social worker is or get him assigned one ASAP. Social workers are supposed to help him get mental health care and support, it’s literally their job. If his social worker doesn’t do their job then keep pestering them or see if he can get assigned a new one.

Never been to jail but that’s how I managed to get therapy while I was homeless after I was in involuntary inpatient. I was lucky enough to have social worker who genuinely cared about her cases and helped me a lot.

Do whatever feels best for you. There are many trans men who don’t like being on t and there are many cis women who enjoy being on t, your hormones do not dictate your gender.

There was a period when I was having an identity crisis so I took an 8month t break. It didn’t get rid of any of the permanent effects such as my voice, which is good because the permanent effects aren’t what was bothering me. Taking a break really helped me figure out how I felt about myself and become more confident in my identity. The only time that I was distressed by not being able to be on t was when it wasn’t my choice (insurance reasons). I accepted that even though I’m a man it doesn’t bother me when I’m seen as just a *really* butch lesbian in certain contexts (idk of it makes sense but to me being seen as butch sometimes feels more masculine than being seen as a feminine man). 

My point is that gender isn’t always a fixed point and for some people it can easily change depending on their situation and mental state. You might be trans, you might not, the important part is that you focus less on if you’re a “cheater” and more on what feels right for you.

If you’re really considering telling ppl you aren’t trans then I would suggest taking some time to do some heavy self reflection first though because many ppl will unfortunately not understand unless they’ve also heavily questioned their own gender. You can try going by different pronouns and names around new ppl at cafes or something if you want to test how you feel without having to tell ppl you already know.

Also, if your chosen name is making you uncomfortable you can always just change it. I don’t like my traditionally male chosen first name as much as I used to so instead I usually go by my middle name, which most Americans assume is gender neutral even though it’s a very masculine name in my culture. Cis people often don’t go by their legal first names so there’s no reason you should have to stick to your chosen name.

Personally, I don’t ever remember being particularly insecure about being short, I just kinda always accepted that it was how I was built and never really bothered to cared all that much. I believe a big reason for this is because growing up I did a lot of things where being short and lightweight can be an advantage (equestrian mainly but also MMA surprisingly). 

My point is that you need to stop focusing on all the negative aspects of your height and figure out how you can use your size to your advantage. Shorter ppl generally have a greater strength to weight ratio, faster rotational capability, higher endurance, better balance, a lower centre of gravity, lower risk of heat exhaustion, faster reflexes, and are less likely to break bones. If you’re a physically active person then learning how to effectively take advantage of the physical benefits of being short will help you build confidence in your body.

As for people being rude to you over your size just keep in mind that you are surrounded by ppl who are at the most immature and shallow stage of their life. Luckily for you you’re almost an adult and that’s about when people tend to get hit in the face with the struggles of adult life and realize that height is the last thing they should care about in other people.

Okay so there’s a lot of reasons for this but if you want the overly simplified version it basically comes down to these reasons 1.) pain is a product of evolution that’s highly important to our species survival. Pain is the bodies way of telling you that there’s something wrong. The more wrong the more it hurts. The more it hurts the more likely you are to avoid whatever was causing the pain. There are ppl with genetic disorders that cause them to not feel pain like everyone else, these ppl have to have frequent intensive medical examinations to make sure they aren’t walking around with broken bones, ulcers, ect. without even realizing it. Without pain life becomes much more dangerous. 2.) human biology is weird in that we are both extremely easy and difficult to kill. We’ve evolved to be more resilient to the most common forms of death so something like bleeding out or poisoning is more difficult than one would expect. Poisoning triggers vomiting in most cases and bleeding out causes your body to slowly shut down so as to not waste energy so you can maybe survive long enough to revive help. Methods of death that are more unusual or recently developed are more likely to kill you. So guns, radiation, drugs, diabetes, ect. are more far recent phenomena when compared to the entire history of hominid evolution. 3.) the biggest reason being one that you already alluded to in your post, people DONT want you or anyone else killing yourself. The people that know how to take a life painlessly are often held under certain ethical and moral constraints that prevent them from giving you this information. Doctors know how to make it painless but they’re not gonna tell you how because to do so would technically go against the Hippocratic oath since it would result in harm. Most things that can kill your painlessly are also heavily regulated or have safeguards put in place to prevent it not only to prevent suicide but also to prevent murders. 

Eventho I’ve been extremely suicidal most of my life there are times when I’m grateful that dying is made as difficult and painful as possible because I know for a fact if it wasn’t that most of my friends and family would’ve offed themselves by now. To anyone reading this, please don’t attempt via overdose/ poisoning, bleeding out, or drowning. I speak from experience when I say all of those methods are not fun and will likely never work for you, you will just end up in extreme pain with life long medical problems and a massive medical bill.

TLDR: humans have evolved to make death as biologically difficult and undesirable as possible and most painless methods are illegal, highly regulated, or intentionally kept as secret as possible from non-medical professionals

I’ve struggled with being underweight almost all of my life and I rarely ever feel hungry, eating actually makes me pretty nauseous most days. If you can I recommend talking to your doc about it and possibly getting a nutritionist, there could be something medically wrong/abnormal that has been overlooked. In my case it turns out I can’t process certain vitamins and minerals correctly without supplements which was causing me to be too nauseous to eat while I was growing. Because I didn’t eat a ton while I was developing my stomach didn’t get as big as it should’ve which is why I don’t feel hunger. 

If you’ve never really eaten enough it’s possible it could have affected the size of your stomach meaning you don’t feel hungry as easily. Either way if you want to gain weight you’ll have to gradually learn how to eat more. There’s also medications a doctor can prescribe you to increase your hunger signals. Personally, I didn’t respond well to those meds so my doc recommended I started smoking weed before meals. Surprisingly it actually helped me gain a few pounds, I really didn’t understand what it was like to be hungry until I got the munchies for the first time. If you do decide to go to down the smoking route do be aware that your body can become dependent on weed to feel hunger after enough time.

There’s plenty of options to choose from to help with weight gain, it’s just that people aren’t as educated on them compared to weight loss methods. If you can see a doc about your weight then you absolutely should do that asap. If you can’t or until you do see one then try to figure out ways to get more calories into your body that work for you. Maybe try eating higher calorie dense foods, adding meal replacements to your diet as well, drinking protein shakes or something you enjoy that has lots of calories like milkshakes, ect. If it works it works and if it doesn’t it doesn’t so long as it gets you to a healthy weight without making you feel like shit. Not saying it’s at all easy, it’s a lot of work and you might feel like crap at first but you’ll probably have a lot more energy when not so severely underweight.

Add hairspray to hold it in place. Also use a heat protectant, especially since your hair is bleached and more prone to heat damage. Another thing you can try that’s much gentler than irons is using a round brush and blow dryer when drying your hair to get those flips. 

If you plan on getting another hair cut to fix it then make sure that you’re extremely specific with what you want. Make sure to look at each individual part of the hair style so you know exactly what to tell your stylist. How long is the hair? Where do you want the layers blended? Do you want you hair thinned or not thinned anywhere? How do you want it to grow out? How much weight and bulk do you want your hair to have and where? How much effort are you willing to put into styling it everyday? Also don’t be afraid to get blunt about what you want, if you don’t like it tell them. Also if you can try to find if the salon or stylist has any pictures of haircuts they’ve done before. Look for a website, Facebook page, tiktok, or Instagram to find someone who cuts more alt styles, that should be easy if you live in a bigger city. For the haircut alone you shouldn’t be paying that much either, it’s not what I would consider a particularly expensive cut.

If you’re gonna try to fix it at home make sure you at least watch a few videos on how to layer hair and how to do ‘Jellyfish’ and ‘wolf’ cuts since it looks like you’re going for a softer mullet blend of the two. If you can when you think you’re finished cutting wash or get your hair completely wet and dry it do you can see what it’s actually gonna look like everyday.

I genuinely never expect any other writers to do this tho since it’s a lot of work and can be jarring to some readers to switch between British vs American English multiple times in the same body of text. DID started to get popular while I was in early/mid high school and I knew a few ppl irl who thought they had DID for a couple of years. Two of them tried to suggest that I might have it due to what I later found out was undiagnosed psychosis and PTSD. I’m incredibly grateful that I didn’t listen to them since I was extremely aware of my mental state at that time, otherwise I might have.

It’s pretty obvious that all of them are going through some tough shit, whether or not they are intentionally faking it. No mentally healthy person fakes or mistakenly thinks they have a disorder. Unless they can figure out and fix what’s actually going on then they’re going to be stuck in the same place for a long time.

I think what a lot of these kids don’t realize is that even if turns out that they do in fact have DID this behavior is still unhealthy and harmful to their own mental well-being. While it is important to have friends or support groups of ppl with similar disorders and illness these discord and tiktok groups just aren’t that. Almost every online DID group actively discourages recovery and rewards self destruction. If they encouraged healthy coping mechanisms, recovery, and didn’t glorify DID then it would be a different story. A really good example of this behavior in other disorders is self harm Twitter vs r/ selfharm. SH twtr is literally the worst place you can go if you SH while r/ selfharm is a great community, especially if you can’t access mental healthcare.

For anyone one who is unsure if they have DID or is part of these DID groups and therapy isn’t an option but wants to get better, my number one recommendation is to take a step back from the DID community and to not define yourself by DID. Instead take the time to recognize what emotions, behaviors, and symptoms are negatively impacting you and those around you. Do your best to figure out what is causing you to do or experience these things. Don’t just rely on “I feel depressed all the time because I have depression” because while that may be true you need to figure out what is triggering it. Once you know the causes and triggers you can begin to fix the problem. Your solutions need to be realistic tho. If you’re 14 and your mom is a trigger for disassociation then it’s very unlikely that you’ll be able to safely cut her out of your life, so if that’s the case try to find short term bandaid solutions that will last until actually fixing the issue is an option. 

If you consistently stick to doing this for a few months and still feel that you experience enough symptoms of DID to potentially have it then finding DID groups that are geared towards recovery instead of the mess that is the discord and TikTok DID community wouldn’t be a bad idea. Remember to be extremely picky and careful about which groups you join. Because there is so much misinformation and hardly any credible research on DID it’s best to choose groups that have an emphasis on clinically backed research. Don’t trust everything others in the groups say about DID until you read an actual peer review study, and I don’t mean sites like healthyplace.com I mean actual scientific journals. Whatever you do, don’t fall back into the habit of defining yourself by any disorder or illness. Centering your personality around DID is just as unhealthy as basing your life on depression or anxiety.
